summary: Dave Richard's CBSSports.com Week 6 fantasy football column (published Oct. 12, 2023) goes game by game with start, sit, flex and sleeper calls backed by matchup, film, coverage and usage data. Calls include sitting Jaleel McLaughlin, Terry McLaurin, K.J. Osborn, Jonathan Taylor, Amari Cooper, Rhamondre Stevenson, Emari Demercado and Dak Prescott, while starting Brock Purdy, Logan Thomas, Cole Kmet, Zack Moss, Jeff Wilson and Justice Hill. Each blurb compares the player to alternatives and cites coverage tendencies, snap shares and defensive stats.
one_line: Dave Richard's Week 6 2023 fantasy football guide gives game-by-game start, sit, flex and sleeper recommendations backed by matchup, film and usage stats.
key_facts: Jaleel McLaughlin (DEN rookie RB) is a sit at Kansas City (KC -10.5, O/U 47); he made three splash plays of 21, 22 and 38 yards against the Jets but his other nine touches each failed to exceed 3 yards.

When Denver has trailed by eight or more points, Samaje Perine has played 58 of 117 snaps, more than McLaughlin (26) and Javonte Williams (27) combined; McLaughlin averages 6.1 yards per carry in that situation.
Zay Flowers (BAL) is a flex starter in PPR at Tennessee (BAL -4, O/U 41); he saw a season-high 11 targets at Pittsburgh but caught five for 73 yards with two drops, and had a 15.27 ADOT.

Justice Hill (BAL) is a sneaky sleeper; across Weeks 1, 2 and 5 he played 24 of 43 third-down snaps (56%) and 14 of 20 snaps inside the 10, and the Titans allowed 6.3 yards per carry to Zack Moss and the Colts.
Terry McLaurin (WAS) is a sit at Atlanta (ATL -2.5, O/U 42.5); he has 31 targets to Jahan Dotson's 30 and Curtis Samuel's 27, and saw only five targets against Chicago's zone last week.

Logan Thomas (WAS TE) is a start at Atlanta, whose defense gives up the third-most targets per game to tight ends (9.0) and the most first-down receptions to the position (17); he saw 10 of 11 targets after the Bears built a 17-point lead.

Kyle Pitts (ATL TE) had season highs of 11 targets, seven catches and 87 yards last week but played a season-low 53% of snaps; his 11.72 ADOT is the highest among qualifying tight ends and his catch rate (56.3%) is the lowest.
K.J. Osborn (MIN WR) is a sit at Chicago, which plays zone at the fourth-highest rate (79.2%); Justin Jefferson is out, and Osborn has a 50% catch rate this year.

Cole Kmet (CHI TE) is a start; since Chase Claypool left he averages seven targets per game with a 24.6% target share and leads Chicago in red-zone targets, and Khalil Herbert and Roschon Johnson are expected to be out.

Jonathan Taylor (IND RB) played 16% of snaps to Zack Moss' 80% in his return and just three second-half snaps; Moss is a start at Jacksonville (JAC -4, O/U 44.5) with up to 15 touches projected versus Taylor's 10.

Brock Purdy (SF QB) is a start at Cleveland; he threw four touchdowns on 24 attempts against Dallas and has hit at least 20 fantasy points in 9 of 10 regular-season starts, while the Browns play the least zone coverage in the league.
Amari Cooper (CLE WR) is a sit with P.J. Walker starting at QB; no team allows fewer yards per catch to wideouts than the 49ers (9.7), and only three receivers have topped 15 PPR points against them.

Jeff Wilson (MIA RB) is a sneaky sleeper vs. Carolina (MIA -13.5, O/U 48.5) after practicing following finger and abdomen injuries, with rookie De'Von Achane on injured reserve with a knee injury; the Panthers rank bottom five in yards per carry allowed to RBs (5.2).

Dak Prescott (DAL QB) is a sit at the Chargers (DAL -2.5, O/U 51); his ADOT is 6.5, 28th of 33 qualifying QBs, he threw interceptions in a blowout loss to the 49ers, and ex-offensive coordinator Kellen Moore now coaches the Chargers offense.
